commit.message:
AMI: Add Command authorizations overlap note to sample configuration

The AMI write command potentially allows users to execute CLI commands
that perform similar operations to actions in other classes.  Update
the sample configuration file to note this.

Resolves: #2238

files.patch:
@@ -295,8 +295,16 @@ Both Legacy and Advanced filter entries are processed as follows:
 ; Authorization for various classes
 ;
 ; Read authorization permits you to receive asynchronous events, in general.
-; Write authorization permits you to send commands and get back responses.  The
-; following classes exist:
+; Write authorization permits you to send actions and get back responses.
+; Read authorization does not restrict information returned in action responses.
+;
+; Class authorizations overlap and are not independent security boundaries.
+; In particular, write=command (also included in write=all) lets a user run CLI
+; commands, such as "channel originate" or "module reload", that perform
+; similar operations to actions in other classes. Grant command only to users
+; trusted with those operations.
+;
+; The following classes exist:
 ;
 ; all       - All event classes below (including any we may have missed).
 ; system    - General information about the system and ability to run system
@@ -311,7 +319,7 @@ Both Legacy and Advanced filter entries are processed as follows:
 ;             members to a queue.
 ; user      - Permission to send and receive UserEvent.
 ; config    - Ability to read and write configuration files.
-; command   - Permission to run CLI commands.  Write-only.
+; command   - Permission to run CLI commands.  Write-only.  See note above.
 ; dtmf      - Receive DTMF events.  Read-only.
 ; reporting - Ability to get information about the system.
 ; cdr       - Output of cdr_manager, if loaded.  Read-only.

data.body:

the release of Certified asterisk-22.8-cert5.

The release artifacts are available for immediate download at  
https://github.com/asterisk/asterisk/releases/tag/certified-22.8-cert5
and
https://downloads.asterisk.org/pub/telephony/certified-asterisk

Repository: https://github.com/asterisk/asterisk

and would have not been possible without your participation.

Thank You!
